title: "Multiple Linear regression"
author: "Shalom Dauphin"
date: "2026-11-10"
output: html_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```


```{r cars}
# 1. Load and look at the data
data(mtcars)
head(mtcars)
str(mtcars)
summary(mtcars[, c("mpg", "wt", "hp")])

# 2. Explore relationships
cor(mtcars[, c("mpg", "wt", "hp")])

# Scatterplot matrix (bigger, clearer)
png("pairs_plot.png", width = 2000, height = 2000, res = 250)
pairs(mtcars[, c("mpg", "wt", "hp")],
      pch = 19, col = "steelblue",
      cex = 1.3, cex.labels = 2)
dev.off()

pairs(mtcars[, c("mpg", "wt", "hp")],
      pch = 19, col = "steelblue",
      cex = 1.3, cex.labels = 2)   # also show it on screen

# 3. Fit the multiple linear regression
model <- lm(mpg ~ wt + hp, data = mtcars)
summary(model)
confint(model)

# 4. Check assumptions

# 4a. Save all four diagnostic plots as one large, clear image
png("diagnostics.png", width = 2400, height = 2000, res = 250)
par(mfrow = c(2, 2), mar = c(5, 5, 4, 2))
plot(model,
     id.n = 1,          # label only the most extreme point
     cex = 1.4,         # bigger points
     cex.lab = 1.3,     # axis label size
     cex.main = 1.5,    # title size
     cex.axis = 1.2,    # tick label size
     cex.id = 1,        # point label size
     pch = 19,          # solid points
     col = "steelblue",
     lwd = 2)
dev.off()
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))

# 4b. Show each diagnostic plot full size on screen (press Enter or use the
#     back arrow in the RStudio Plots pane to move between them)
plot(model, which = 1, id.n = 1, pch = 19, col = "steelblue", cex = 1.4)  # Residuals vs Fitted
plot(model, which = 2, id.n = 1, pch = 19, col = "steelblue", cex = 1.4)  # Q-Q
plot(model, which = 3, id.n = 1, pch = 19, col = "steelblue", cex = 1.4)  # Scale-Location
plot(model, which = 5, id.n = 1, pch = 19, col = "steelblue", cex = 1.4)  # Residuals vs Leverage

# 4c. Multicollinearity and normality tests
install.packages("car")   # only needed once
library(car)
vif(model)           # multicollinearity (values under ~5 are fine)

shapiro.test(residuals(model))   # normality of residuals

# Where were the images saved?
getwd()
```
